summary: Backend-only testing for Undangan Digital. Wrote 20 pytest tests in /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py covering: health, templates (list + wedding filter), auth (unauthenticated 401 + Bearer-header seeded session), event CRUD (create/list/get/patch/delete-cascade), guest bulk creation with unique slugs, Xendit-mock checkout, mock payment completion (publishes event), free-tier publish, WhatsApp bulk send (mocked, requires published), public invitation retrieval + 404 for draft events, RSVP submit + summary counts, and real Emergent Object Storage upload/download. All 20 tests pass after fixing a bug in POST /api/events. Seeded test user+session directly in MongoDB via pymongo (per /app/memory/test_credentials.md).
action_items: None - all endpoints working. One implementation bug was auto-fixed (see rca).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py POST /api/events originally had extra `user: dict = None` param before Cookie/Header params. FastAPI treated `user` as a required body field, wrapping the request under {payload:..., user:...} and returning 422 for normal payloads. Fixed by removing the stray parameter.
Auth logic is duplicated across ~15 endpoints (session_token cookie + authorization header + call get_current_user). Recommend using FastAPI Depends(get_current_user) to DRY this up.
server.py is ~660 lines - approaching the 700-line threshold. Consider splitting into routers/models/services modules.
`get_current_user` doesn't refresh/rotate session tokens; expired tokens are only detected but not cleaned from DB.
`slugify` returns generic prefix `e-xxxxxx` on empty input which is fine, but event slug uniqueness relies on random 4-hex suffix rather than DB-checked uniqueness - collision risk (~1/65k).
Public GET /api/public/inv/{slug} strips user_id but the event object still contains internal fields like config with private notes - acceptable for MVP but review for future.

rsvp_summary uses `counts[g['rsvp_status']]` - if a guest ever has an unexpected status string it would raise KeyError (mitigated by the default insert value but no server-side validation prevents direct DB corruption).
updated_files: /app/backend/server.py (removed stray `user: dict = None` param from create_event)
test_credentials: No password-based creds. Test seeds `users` + `user_sessions` rows in MongoDB `test_database`; the Bearer token is passed via `Authorization: Bearer <session_token>`.
seed_data_creation: Session-scoped pytest fixture inserts a test user and session directly via pymongo, tears down after tests. Tests also create+delete events/guests/payments/files during runs.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend suite is at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py, executed via `pytest` from /app/backend (pytest.ini pins xdist -n 2 loadscope, keep the whole module in one file to preserve module-scoped fixture sharing). All 20 tests currently green. Emergent Object Storage upload works end-to-end. Frontend was NOT tested per request.
rca of the issue: POST /api/events was returning 422 `body.payload field required`. Root cause: the handler signature included `user: dict = None` between the Pydantic body param and the Cookie/Header params. FastAPI treats a bare `dict`-typed param without explicit Query/Header/Depends binding as an additional body field; the presence of two body fields (payload, user) makes FastAPI wrap the request as `{"payload": {...}, "user": ...}`. Fix: removed `user: dict = None` from create_event signature (the function already fetches the user via get_current_user inside the body). Verified by re-running the suite - all 20 tests pass.
